analysis.title: European Conference Day Two: ECB Leadership, French Politics, China-EU Trade
key_insights: Panelists at the UBS European Conference see former Dutch central bank chief Klaas Knot as the most likely next ECB president despite having no French endorsement. Support from Paris could secure it for him.

Christine Lagarde steps down on Feb. 7, giving EU leaders time to pick a successor before a French presidential election that polls show Marine Le Pen is favoured to win. The Netherlands has nominated Knot and Spain has nominated Pablo Hernández de Cos.
Reuters has reported that France would back Knot provided the ECB chief economist post goes to a French candidate.

France is running out of money and time. The government will miss its deficit target and France's borrowing premium over Germany has widened to the most since 2012. Panelists said the ECB would ideally look to prop up France.

Marine Le Pen leads the French presidential race by about 10pp in second-round polling. She is most trusted on immigration, cost of living and public services, which panelists said can be more predictive of an election outcome than polls.

In the recent US midterms, polling underplayed Democratic support, but the party was ahead on the key issues by margins close to the final result. The French cordon sanitaire this time appears aimed at far-left LFI candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon rather than the RN.

Panelists said Le Pen is unlikely to moderate her anti-EU positions if elected and may try to pull Italy's Giorgia Meloni back into the nationalist camp. Clashes are possible over EU spending, Ukraine, sanctions, defense and migration. Market pressure may be the main source of leverage for moderation.

The China-EU trade imbalance has grown sharply. China sent 6.2 containers to Europe for every one it received, up from 2.75 four years ago. The EU exports more to Switzerland than to China, and Germany is losing 10,000 jobs a month in industry.
China is looking at voluntary export restrictions and boosting imports, but panelists said it is unclear how effective these will be.

Chinese domestic consumption is hard to lift because households save for old age. Policymakers see strong exports and decent GDP and feel no urgency, while exports are strong because domestic demand is weak.

Panelists expect China to concede enough to Europe to avoid a trade war before 2027, a Communist Party congress year. More deals like the hybrids deal could follow. BYD and other exporters rely on profitable markets like Europe.

Corporate presentations on day one pointed to resilient but uneven growth, persistent inflationary pressure and reliance on productivity to drive earnings. European activity appears to be stabilising, and earnings growth may outpace economic growth.
A former Democratic Senator said Democrats are not anti-data centre but want tech companies to consult local communities and address energy use and residential power prices.

For the Republican nomination, much depends on whether Trump endorses JD Vance. Panelists said Republicans have work to do given that the same party has held the presidency after two terms only once since 1988, and given the midterm results.

Speakers said the US is pulling away from Europe on productivity and growth. They credited faster US labour-market adjustment after Covid, versus European furlough schemes that froze parts of those economies.

Panelists said Trump will keep pushing AI and that federal regulation is needed, while governors and mayors push back locally. Data centers will need to explain how they pay for their own utilities and frame the build-out as national security.

With Democrats holding majorities in both houses, panelists expect bipartisan opportunities, starting with a bill banning members of Congress and the president from trading stocks, then restoring Medicaid cuts.
A panelist said the UAE's departure hurt OPEC but did not collapse it. OPEC's future depends on Saudi Arabia, which is unlikely to leave. The UAE could return later.

A speaker said the energy system has been more resilient to recent shocks than expected. Hormuz disruption had less impact because more oil was available and Chinese demand weakened. Parts of Asia faced greater pressure.

A speaker said the path to oil normalisation will be bumpier than the forward curve prices. Freight costs and refining capacity come first. US refinery utilisation is around 93% and others near 100%, so maintenance could rise next year. Another speaker said normalisation could take a year after the conflict ends.
Private markets panelists see AI-driven healthcare and life sciences as a major opportunity over five to 10 years, and US affordable housing as a $200 bn opportunity.
Crédit Agricole's proposed merger of Crédit Agricole Italia and BAMI was the key focus of its session, with financial and capital details expected as talks progress.
Eni expects capex around €7 bn a year including €400-500 mn of exploration, has discovered over 1.2 bn boe this year, and expects FID on Venezuela's Junín-5 by year-end or early next year.
EDP said earnings are running ahead of expectations after three guidance upgrades this year. US renewables returns are 9-10% unlevered IRR and leverage is c.3x ND/EBITDA.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The market is pricing France's fiscal slippage and political risk, and the deficit target will be missed.

macro_indicators.indicator: France presidential second-round polling, Le Pen lead
macro_indicators.interpretation: Le Pen is favoured, which raises political risk for French assets.
The trade imbalance has more than doubled from 2.75 four years ago.
Refineries are run hard, so maintenance could rise next year and slow oil normalisation.
The China-EU imbalance is hollowing out Europe's industrial base.

risk_factors: France misses its deficit target while its borrowing premium over Germany is the widest since 2012.
A Le Pen presidency could bring clashes with the EU over spending, Ukraine, sanctions, defense and migration.
The China-EU trade imbalance and Chinese overcapacity could escalate into a trade war.
Oil normalisation could be slower than the forward curve prices because of freight, refining capacity and maintenance.
Local backlash to data centers over power use and prices could slow the US AI build-out.
Weak European growth and productivity are widening the gap with the US.
geopolitical: Klaas Knot is seen as the likely next ECB president, with Netherlands and Spain nominating candidates and France's position pending.
Marine Le Pen is favoured in the 2027 French presidential election and is unlikely to moderate her anti-EU positions.
China-EU trade tensions are rising, with China likely to concede enough to avoid a trade war before the 2027 Communist Party congress.
Disruption around Hormuz had less impact than expected, and a conflict is ongoing that could take another year to normalise after it concludes.
The UAE has left OPEC, and Saudi Arabia is expected to stay.
US midterm results point to a centrist shift nationally, with Democrats holding both houses.
